scope.claim: All stop-hook variants (Python/shell/other, all severity markers ✅/❌/⚠️/⛔) share the literal 'Stop hook feedback:' prefix emitted by Claude Code CLI.
scope.verification: Empirical scan confirms all 369 real records start with exactly 'Stop hook feedback:\n[<script>]: \n<body>'. The prefix comes from the Claude Code CLI itself (not the individual hook scripts), which means it is invariant across hook implementations. A single startsWith('Stop hook feedback:') check catches 100% of observed variants.
scope.coverage_gaps: Only Python hooks observed in production data. BA acknowledges shell/other scripts in scope but relies on the CLI-level prefix invariant. This is structurally sound — the prefix is injected by the Claude Code runtime wrapping hook output, not by the hook itself, so shell/bash/other hooks would produce the same prefix.
scope.edge_case_false_positive: BA acknowledges the risk: a legitimate user message starting literally with 'Stop hook feedback:' would be swallowed. This is acceptable — users do not type this as the start of a message. Matches the risk profile of existing 'API Error:' and '[Request interrupted' filters.
scope.edge_case_partial_match_preserved: BA's AC3 explicitly preserves 'About stop hook feedback: this is a comment' as a real user message because startsWith (not contains) is used. This matches existing patterns.

summary: BA spec §5.9 is sound and cleared for implementation. All four dimensions (evidence, scope, investigation, file_accuracy) pass verification. Wire format claim verified against 369 real records across 11270 JSONL files — all are type:'user' with string content starting with 'Stop hook feedback:\n[<script>]: \n<body>'. The single 'Stop hook feedback:' prefix check proposed by BA catches 100% of observed variants (3 different hook scripts, including severity marker ⛔) because the prefix is injected by the Claude Code CLI itself, not by individual hook scripts. File path sessionProtocolMapper.ts:855 and function getSystemInjectedServiceText() confirmed byte-accurate. Caller semantics at lines 674-678 confirmed — returning non-null from the function causes empty envelopes emission (silent drop). Only minor objection: BA cites a specific JSONL file that contains 0 actual stop-hook records, but this does not invalidate the conclusion (evidence exists elsewhere).

implementation_guidance_to_dev.exact_change: Add one if-branch in sessionProtocolMapper.ts getSystemInjectedServiceText() BEFORE line 878 (isMeta check) and BEFORE line 882 (final return null). Suggested insertion point: after line 874 (API Error: branch) and before line 878 (isMeta check).
implementation_guidance_to_dev.rationale: Returning null causes the caller at line 676-677 to emit zero envelopes. Matches the behavior for <task-notification>, [Request interrupted, Failed to start session, API Error: (all existing silent-drop paths when their semantic label is not surfaced — note that these return a string which also results in empty envelopes at line 677, but returning null is cleaner because no service envelope is ever contemplated for stop-hook).
implementation_guidance_to_dev.caveat_re_return_semantics: BA specifies return null (not a service label like 'Stop hook feedback'). This is correct: returning any non-null value from getSystemInjectedServiceText() causes the caller to return empty envelopes — but the function's contract says non-null means 'system-injected with this service label'. Since no service envelope is actually emitted from the caller (lines 676-678 just return envelopes as-is), both null and a string would achieve the same silent-drop effect. Returning null is simply more semantically honest ('not a system-injected text we want to surface'). Dev should return null, not a string.
